privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Screen Shield is an independent student-built project by Kabir Anand. This policy describes the Mac app and its download page. Acknowledging this policy does not waive your privacy rights.

sections.title: 1. Camera and screen information stays local
sections.body:
When enabled, Screen Shield processes webcam frames, face landmarks, face positions, and head-orientation estimates in your Mac’s memory to decide when to show a privacy cover. It does not enroll identities, create an identity database, or try to identify people by name.

When the cover is needed, the app briefly holds a screenshot in memory, blurs it, and displays the frozen image. Screen Shield does not save or transmit webcam frames, face images, or screenshots. In-memory processing is not a promise of secure memory erasure by Python or macOS.

If you open optional Model view, the app displays the live camera locally with colored face boxes and head-angle estimates for testing. This opt-in display is not recorded or transmitted. The privacy cover is suppressed while Model view is open, including during a camera outage.

sections.title: 2. Permissions and controls
sections.body:
The app requests Camera access for local detection and Screen Recording access for its in-memory screen cover. The optional global shortcut uses local keyboard events; the app does not record or upload keystrokes. Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission may be needed. You can use the app buttons if the shortcut is unavailable.

Disabling or quitting releases the webcam. Snoozing pauses processing but may keep an already-open camera allocated, so its light can remain on. You can revoke permissions through macOS System Settings.

Opening Model view while disabled temporarily enables the camera for testing. Closing it restores the previous enabled or disabled setting; if previously disabled, the camera is released. Model view continues processing during a protection snooze so you can test the model.

sections.title: 3. Files stored on your Mac
sections.body:
The app stores preferences, a small acceptance record containing the policy version, document checksum and acceptance time, and library cache data on your Mac. These are not video recordings. The packaged Mac app uses ~/Library/Application Support/Screen Shield/. The acceptance record is not sent to the developer.

Optional debug output contains numeric face sizes, head angles, states, and technical errors. The app does not install a file logger. macOS or third-party runtimes may create their own crash or diagnostic records under your system settings. Screen Shield does not automatically send those records to the developer.

If you record your own evaluation clips with another app, Screen Shield can read those local files for testing; it does not upload them or save extracted frames.

sections.title: 4. Download-page storage and hosting
sections.body:
The supplied download page contains no analytics, advertising scripts, remote fonts, accounts, or camera access. It uses browser local storage, when available, to remember acceptance of this policy and the Terms of Service. You can remove that record by clearing this site’s browser storage. If storage is unavailable, acceptance applies only to the current page session.

If this page or its downloads are hosted online, the hosting provider may receive ordinary requests, IP addresses, browser information and download metadata under that provider’s policies. That hosting traffic is separate from the local app; no camera or screen content is included. Following an external link, such as Apple’s installation guidance, is subject to that site’s practices.

sections.title: 5. Your choices and other people
sections.body:
You can decline the policies and leave the app unopened, disable detection, quit, revoke macOS permissions, or uninstall. To remove local preferences and the acceptance record after quitting, remove the Screen Shield folder in your user Application Support directory. Delete browser storage separately if desired.

Use the camera only where you have permission and consider the privacy of people nearby. Screen Shield is not designed to identify or profile children or other individuals. It has no user-account registration or intentional collection of information for the developer.

sections.title: 6. Changes and contact
sections.body:
If these documents change, their version/checksum changes and the supplied download page and app ask for acceptance again. Review a new version before accepting.

For privacy questions, contact Kabir Anand at screenshield.riverboat836@silomails.com. This public address is a forwarding alias. A support email is processed by email/forwarding providers and delivered to the developer’s private mailbox; it is not end-to-end encrypted merely because an alias is used. Do not send camera footage, screenshots, or other sensitive information unless you choose to share it.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms cover the supplied Screen Shield download page and packaged app provided by Kabir Anand. Please read them before choosing to accept. If you do not agree, cancel the download or quit the app.

sections.title: 1. Student-built preview
sections.body:
Screen Shield is an independent student-built, experimental privacy aid. It is not a certified security product, an Apple product, or a guarantee that nobody can see, photograph, record or capture your screen. It is not represented as endorsed by a school or other institution.

This preview is not signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate or notarized by Apple. macOS may block internet-downloaded copies. Student authorship is context, not evidence that software is safe. Only choose to open a copy if you trust its source and have reviewed the risks. Do not disable Gatekeeper globally.

sections.title: 2. Limits of protection
sections.body:
Detection can miss viewers or produce false alerts. It depends on camera placement, lighting, face size, head angle, permissions and hardware. It cannot reliably detect people outside the camera view, a phone filming the screen, reflections, or software screenshots and recording. The cover affects the primary display and may not cover secure system interfaces or every fullscreen space.

Camera loss, a blocked driver, an app crash, a paused process or a native-library problem can interrupt protection. The fail-closed setting is an optional cover policy, not a security guarantee. Do not rely on Screen Shield as your only control for confidential information, workplace requirements, legal obligations or regulated data.

Model view is a testing mode: it intentionally turns the privacy cover off while its window is open. Green is an estimated owner, yellow is another detected face that does not pass viewer checks, and red is a candidate that passes them. These colors do not establish identity, eye gaze, or harmful intent. Close Model view to return to the previous protection setting.

sections.title: 3. Responsible use and permissions
sections.body:
Use the app only on devices you own or are authorized to administer, where camera use and monitoring are permitted. Obtain any permissions required by your school, workplace, household or other applicable rules. Do not use it to stalk, secretly monitor, harass or unlawfully collect information about others.

You control macOS permissions and may revoke them. Accepting these terms does not itself grant Camera, Screen Recording, Accessibility or Input Monitoring access. macOS asks for those permissions separately.

These terms describe use of the supplied app and page; they do not create a paid subscription, automatic renewal, service-level commitment or requirement to purchase anything.

sections.body:
The app and page are provided AS IS and AS AVAILABLE, to the extent permitted by applicable law, without promises of accuracy, uninterrupted availability, suitability for a particular purpose or freedom from bugs. There is no guaranteed support response or maintenance schedule.

To the extent permitted by law, the developer is not responsible for losses caused by missed viewers, false alerts, interruptions, reliance on the app, or use outside its intended scope. Nothing here excludes liability, consumer protections, privacy rights or other rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. This paragraph does not expand the disclaimer in a way that overrides mandatory law.

sections.title: 6. Acceptance, changes and stopping use
sections.body:
The supplied download flow and the first-run app screen ask you to review both documents, acknowledge the Privacy Policy, and explicitly agree to these terms. An acceptance record is stored locally; the app does not send it to the developer. You may stop using the app at any time by disabling, quitting or uninstalling it.

A document update requires renewed acceptance before the updated app starts monitoring. If you disagree with a revision, do not accept it. Contact Kabir Anand at screenshield.riverboat836@silomails.com if you have questions.
